item.title: Shopping malls, markets can stay open until 10pm for Durga Puja
item.description:
The government has extended the operating hours of shopping malls, markets and stores across Bangladesh ahead of Durga Puja 2026, allowing them to remain open from 11am to 10pm until October 22.
The directive was issued on Monday, October 5, 2026, through an office order signed by Sonia Binte Tabib, deputy secretary of the Electricity Division’s Coordination-2 branch under the Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources.
According to the order, shopping malls, markets and stores can remain open daily from 11am to 10pm until October 22.
From October 23, the previous schedule of 11am to 8pm will resume and remain in effect.
Copies of the order have been sent to the mayors or administrators of all city corporations, divisional commissioners, deputy commissioners and other relevant offices for necessary action.

item.title: Man shot dead in Khulna 50 days after son’s murder
item.description:
A man was shot dead in Khulna’s Rupsa upazila on Monday evening, 50 days after his son was shot and hacked to death in the same area.
The deceased was identified as Aktar Dhali, 64, of Durjani Mahal village under Aichgati union. The incident occurred around 6:45pm, when Aktar was sitting on a bench beside the road in front of his house.
Family members said they suddenly heard gunshots and came outside to find Aktar lying beside the bench. Unidentified assailants had shot him before fleeing the scene.
Doctors at Khulna Medical College Hospital declared him dead after he was taken there.
Murad Hossain, an emergency department staff member at Khulna Medical College Hospital, said Aktar had been shot in his right shoulder. He may also have sustained injuries from shotgun pellets.
Rupsa Police Station Officer-in-Charge Anwar Zahid said: “Police have been sent to the place where Aktar Dhali was shot. We are investigating who carried out the incident and why. The body is being processed for autopsy.”
He said: “Police have started investigating to identify and arrest those involved in the killing. We will also examine whether there is any connection between the 2 killings.”
Aktar’s son Joy Dhali, 27, was shot and hacked to death in the same area on August 15.
Police said a group of 4-5 people attacked Joy in front of Durjani Mahal in the Shaheed Mor area of Rupsa around 8:30pm that day. The helmeted assailants arrived on motorcycles and hacked him, killing him at the scene before fleeing on motorcycles.
The killing of Aktar triggered panic among local residents, while senior police officials visited the scene after receiving the news.
The body is being processed for autopsy, and police are investigating the killing and the possible connection between the 2 incidents.

item.title: Bangladeshi killed in Houthi strike in Saudi Arabia
item.description:
A Bangladeshi national was killed in a missile or drone strike carried out by the Houthis on an Aramco facility in the Al Khurais area of Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province on Sunday, said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Monday.
The deceased was identified as Md Sajib Hossain, a resident of Comilla district. Further details were not immediately available.
The ministry expressed deep shock and sorrow at his death and strongly condemned the attack. It also conveyed its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved family.
It said the Bangladesh Embassy in Saudi Arabia has already contacted the deceased's family and the employer and is providing necessary assistance.
The embassy is coordinating with the relevant Saudi authorities to complete the formalities and arrange for the repatriation of Sajib's body to Bangladesh, the ministry added.

item.title: Idol makers caught between rising costs, shrinking profits
item.description:
With Durga Puja less than two weeks away, idol makers in Dhaka and other parts of the country are working long hours to meet the seasonal rush.
But behind the colorful images taking shape in their workshops lies a harsher reality: the price of idols has risen, yet their profits have not kept pace.
Higher prices of raw materials, rising wages and other costs are eating into their earnings.
Artisans said the growing use of technology is reducing demand for some hand-crafted work, while younger members of their families are reluctant to carry on the traditional profession.
Gopalganj’s Ratan Pal, 54, has spent 26 years making idols.
He learned the craft in Madaripur and is now working at Ramna Kali Temple in Dhaka with five other artisans.
Ratan said an idol that cost Tk 50,000-60,000 to make around a decade ago now costs about Tk 100,000.
But that does not mean his earnings have doubled.
“The price of idols has gone up, but so have the costs of everything else – raw materials, wages and food,” he said.
Six artisans typically work on a single idol, he said. Once their wages and other expenses are paid, little is left for the makers.
And the work is not available throughout the year.
Ratan said idol makers get around 200 to 250 days of work a year, with demand peaking around major festivals.
During the rest of the year, orders are limited.
Technology is also changing the way idols are made.
“Many smaller idols are now made with the help of machines. As a result, there is less work for artisans who make them by hand,” Ratan said.
He acknowledged that technology has made some parts of the process faster and more precise.
Paint, for example, is often applied using sprays before artisans add finishing touches with brushes.
But something is lost in the process, he feels.
“Earlier, every part of an idol was made by hand. We would spend time and care on every detail. That affection and personal touch are not there in the same way anymore,” he said.
For 58-year-old Boloy Pal, the challenge is not only about technology or rising costs. It is also about whether the tradition will survive another generation.
Boloy has been making idols for 38 years, continuing a family tradition that has lasted five generations.
This year, it is taking around three months to complete an idol at Sri Sri Pranaballabh Jiu Temple, where he is working with six other artisans.
Yet none of that guarantees that the craft will continue in his family.
His son is studying in Kolkata and his daughter in the United States. Neither has shown interest in taking up idol-making.
“Idol makers do not get the respect they deserve, and it has become difficult to support a family through this work,” Boloy said. “That is why the younger generation does not want to enter the profession.”
For artisans like Ratan and Boloy, Durga Puja remains the busiest and most important time of the year.
But the few months of activity cannot hide the uncertainty that follows.

item.title: PM stresses teachers’ dignity, modernizing education system
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Monday underscored the need for modernizing the education system, enhancing teachers’ dignity and ensuring their financial security to build a knowledge-based society capable of facing global challenges.
He also called for greater use of technology in education while stressing that artificial intelligence and other technologies should support teachers rather than replace them.
The prime minister made the remarks while addressing a discussion marking World Teachers’ Day 2026 at the Osmani Memorial Auditorium in the capital.
The discussion, organized by the Ministry of Education, highlighted teachers’ dignity, rights, professional development and the need to ensure quality education.
This year’s World Teachers’ Day is being observed under the theme “Standing with Teachers: Sixty Years of Protecting the Profession, Advancing its Status, Shaping our Futures.”
Tarique Rahman congratulated teachers who were recognized on the occasion and paid tribute to teachers from primary schools to universities for their contribution to educating future generations.
He said teachers become students’ role models after they move beyond the family environment and stressed that teachers should be able to present themselves confidently as role models before their students.
The prime minister said the rapid development of social media and artificial intelligence has made it necessary to move beyond traditional education methods.
“Technical and practical education has become essential. Therefore, changing teaching and learning strategies and modernizing the education curriculum have become a necessity of the time,” he said.
Tarique Rahman said the government is working on a new curriculum and hoped that students will receive textbooks based on it this year.
He stressed that students should not merely memories information but should be encouraged to ask questions such as “why” and “how”.
“If students can develop the habit of asking why and how, they can gradually become their own teachers,” the Prime Minister said.
He also highlighted the importance of joyful learning, saying the government has introduced a book titled “Learning with Happiness” for Class VI students for the first time this year, saying the initiative will gradually be extended to other classes.
Tarique Rahman said the education sector is facing both opportunities and challenges amid the rapid advancement of artificial intelligence.
He underlined the need to modernize teacher-training colleges to equip teachers with the skills required to respond to changing educational needs. “We do not want to see technology as a substitute for teachers. Rather, technology will be a tool for teachers,” he said.
The prime minister said the government will advance the “One Teacher, One Tab” program so that teachers could use tablets for digital lesson plans, question banks, monitoring students’ learning progress and accessing educational materials.
The government is also taking initiatives to expand multimedia classes and free Wi-Fi facilities in educational institutions across the country, he said.
Tarique Rahman said the government wants to build an education system where no child will remain deprived of education and no one will have to drop out at any stage of their educational life.
He said education has received the highest priority from the government and that the country has allocated its highest-ever budget for the education sector. “We have plans to increase the education budget further over the next five years to achieve the targets we have set,” he said.
The prime minister sought teachers’ cooperation in implementing the government’s education plans, saying their support will be essential to achieving the targets.
He said the secondary education sector alone has around 21,000 institutions and more than 300,000 teachers, with a large part of the country’s education system dependent on private and MPO-listed institutions.
Tarique Rahman acknowledged disparities in educational opportunities between urban and rural areas and said the government is working to ensure that students everywhere could benefit from qualified teachers and modern technology.
He said the government’s education reform vision is based on equal opportunities, quality education and non-discriminatory access.
The prime minister said employment-oriented education is necessary considering the country’s realities, but employment should not be considered the sole purpose of education.
“Ethics and character building should certainly be the main objectives of education,” he said.
“If knowledge is not connected with morality, that knowledge may become a cause of harm to society instead of contributing to its welfare,” Tarique Rahman said.
He stressed making truthfulness, responsibility, empathy, patriotism, humanity, discipline and respect for others integral parts of education.
The Prime Minister said teachers, after families, could play the most important role in instilling moral values in students.
Tarique Rahman said the government is taking various measures to ensure financial security for teachers, particularly those working at primary, secondary and higher-secondary levels, and to make teaching a competitive profession in terms of opportunities and respect.
“Teaching can never be a last resort or just another ordinary job,” he said.
The prime minister said the government wants talented people to choose teaching as their first career option.
“The dignity of teachers in the state and society is linked to the dignity of the state itself,” he said.
Tarique Rahman also directed the relevant authorities to ensure that, from this year, at least one primary school teacher and one secondary school teacher are invited to state functions marking major national days, including Independence Day and Victory Day.
He said teachers, whether serving or retired, should be honored by the state because of the dignity of their profession.
The prime minister also instructed the relevant ministry to ensure that teachers do not have to visit government offices repeatedly to receive their salaries or retirement benefits.
“A teacher should not have to suffer by going from office to office for their salary or retirement benefits. Their entitled payments must reach them through banks on time and according to the rules,” he said.
Tarique Rahman described teachers as one of the main pillars of building a knowledge-based state and society.
At the program, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman handed over the “Guni Teacher Recognition” awards to 102 distinguished teachers from primary to higher education levels.
Each received a cash award of Tk 200,000, a crest and a certificate of recognition.
The award recipients included late educationist and former Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Prof Emajuddin Ahmed, former Dhaka University Vice-Chancellor Anwarullah Chowdhury and National Professor Dr Mahbub Ullah.
Tarique Rahman congratulated the award recipients and paid tribute to teachers from primary schools to universities.

item.title: TIB urges BNP, Jamaat to strengthen party accountability and end violence
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has called on the leadership of the ruling Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and opposition Jamaat-e-Islami to undertake fundamental reforms and effective self-correction within their respective parties and affiliated organizations to end violent struggles for asserting authority.
The call came after an armed attack and death threats against media workers at Rajshahi University (RU) on the night of October 4, which allegedly involved leaders and activists of Chhatra Dal and left at least 10 people, including 4 journalists, injured.
TIB also condemned the attack and called for justice irrespective of the political identity or influence of those involved.
TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said: “Justice must be ensured for the media workers and students who were attacked. Regardless of their political affiliation or power, the perpetrators of the attack, along with their accomplices and supporters, must be prosecuted and held to a high standard through an unbiased investigation.”
He also called for appropriate medical treatment for the injured, security for media workers and students, and accountability of the police, including an investigation into the reasons for their failure to discharge their duties.
“Attacks on journalists compromise the public’s right to information and limit the ability to hold those in positions of authority responsible; the state must provide remedies for this,” he said.
According to media reports, the university proctor has acknowledged the administration’s failure, while, according to his account, police also fled out of fear. The university administration has announced that it will file a case by October 5, while Chhatra Dal has formed an internal investigation committee.
The journalists have demanded the arrest of those accused and the resignation of the concerned administrative officials.
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the helplessness of the university authorities and the police’s failure to act, including their reported retreat, showed that resolving such power-struggle-driven problems could not depend solely on holding those directly responsible accountable.
“Without fundamental reforms and self-correction within political parties, particularly those in positions of power, not only will the aspirations of the July Uprising remain distant, but fundamental rights - including freedom of the media, freedom of speech and dissent, security of life and livelihood, and equal rights for all citizens - will face increasingly serious threats,” he said.
Calling for specific action by the political leadership, the TIB executive director said the ruling BNP and opposition Jamaat-e-Islami must control their respective parties and affiliated organizations and end violent struggles for asserting authority.
“Rather than considering their responsibility discharged merely by forming investigation committees or taking organizational measures, they must stop providing patronage and protection to violence, ensure an environment conducive to bringing those involved in criminal activities under the law, and establish democratic practices and accountability in party decisions and conduct,” he said.
“Without ensuring such changes within their own organizations, it will not be possible for political parties to earn public trust. Political leaders must realize that they are increasingly detached from the people due to their party leaders’ and activists’ behavior.”
Dr Iftekharuzzaman said the incident could not be viewed in isolation, describing the administration’s failure to stop the attack as part of a larger context of the university’s institutional authority erosion.
“Demands for the resignation of vice-chancellors and teachers, violence over influence on campus, attempts at occupying spaces and institutions, and displays of muscle power at different times have also exposed this institutional weakness,” he said.
He said students’ right to seek justice and peacefully raise their demands must be protected, while allegations against vice-chancellors or teachers should be subject to impartial investigation and due process-based accountability.
“However, party influence, intimidation, or the use of force to enforce demands for resignation cannot be accepted,” he said.
“A situation in which, under political patronage, a section of students becomes so empowered that the university administration is unable to discharge its responsibilities and the police fail to enforce the law cannot be allowed to continue. Universities must be governed by law and regulations, not by the dominance of party power.”
TIB has called for an investigation into the failures of the university authorities and police and for responsibility to be fixed.
The organization said there could be no scope for evading responsibility by citing political pressure or helplessness. The government must ensure that political identity does not become a shield against criminal accountability and that university administrations and law enforcement agencies can discharge their responsibilities independently of partisan influence.

item.title: DSCC clears Segunbagicha footpath of hawkers; adds benches, graffiti
item.description:
The Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has reclaimed a footpath in Segunbagicha from hawkers and reopened it to pedestrians, warning that anyone who returns to the area will face legal action and have their goods seized.
The renovated footpath now features new dustbins, benches for pedestrians and a refurbished boundary wall. As part of the beautification work, graffiti depicting 10 prominent figures from Bangladesh’s art and cultural heritage has also been added, including Shilpacharya Zainul Abedin, filmmaker Satyajit Ray, poet Rabindranath Tagore and National Poet Kazi Nazrul Islam.
DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam inaugurated the beautification work at the reclaimed footpath in Segunbagicha on Monday morning.
“No hawker will be allowed to occupy roads or footpaths in the capital. Alternative designated locations have been arranged for hawkers, and they must conduct their businesses there,” he said at the inauguration.
He warned that hawkers who return to prohibited areas after eviction would face legal action, including the seizure of their goods.
“We do not want to evict anyone, nor do we want poor hawkers to suffer losses to their capital. That is why alternative locations have been designated for them,” Abdus Salam said.
He said a “holiday market” had been arranged at the Pir Yemeni Mazar area on Fridays and Saturdays, while hawkers had been allowed to operate on the footpath along the road opposite Ideal School on other days.
“These decisions were taken through several discussions with leaders of hawker organisations. Hawkers cannot block the main road or set up stalls on any other footpath without permission,” he said.
The administrator said the area, which had previously been difficult for pedestrians to use, had been freed from hawker encroachment through sustained efforts.
“We want to develop this area adjacent to the Bangladesh Shilpakala Academy as a clean cultural environment,” he said.
He said DSCC cleaners would regularly maintain the area, while the Shilpakala Academy and citizens would also have to play a responsible role in preserving its cleanliness and appearance.
Calling for cooperation from journalists, hawkers and residents to keep Dhaka clean, green and beautiful, Abdus Salam said maintaining a “clean and green” capital was not solely the government’s responsibility.
“It is the civic responsibility of all Dhaka residents to keep Dhaka clean and green,” he said.

item.title: Maya Ride offers women-only transport option in Dhaka
item.description:
For many women in Dhaka, travelling around the city can be stressful, especially when using crowded public transport or riding on motorcycles with male drivers.
A new transport platform, Maya Ride, is trying to offer an alternative by connecting female passengers with verified female riders.
Launched in mid-April 2026 by Fahad Chowdhury and Jannatul Ferdous, Maya Ride provides women-only bike and scooter rides, car services and pre-booked transportation for school-going children.
Within its first four months, around 70 female motorcycle riders joined the platform, with about 30 active riders. Around 25 female car drivers also joined, while four to five were regularly providing rides. More than 300 motorcycle rides were completed during the period, according to the founders.
The idea came from Jannatul's own experience and observations of women's daily travel in Dhaka.
“I used to think that I probably wouldn't feel comfortable either if I were in that situation. That thought really stayed with me,” Jannatul said, referring to women travelling on motorcycles with male riders.
Fahad said the initiative initially started as an experiment.
“Since I have been working in data marketing for eight years, I thought I would run an experiment,” he said.
The platform mainly works through pre-booked rides. Passengers provide their pickup and destination details, and Maya Ride matches them with an available female rider. The company says riders and companions go through identity and background verification before being assigned to bookings.
One regular passenger is Nuzhat Tabassum, a resident of Shyamoli who travels to her office in Gulshan-1. She has used Maya Ride more than 30 times.
“It is true that the cost is somewhat higher than Pathao or Uber. But considering how safe I feel here and how I can travel without worrying, I would say the extra cost is worth it,” she said.
Safety and comfort are also highlighted in customer reviews published on Maya Ride's website.
Sadia Toha wrote that she felt safe and secure during her ride and appreciated the initiative.
Another customer, Mehrin Akter, described her experience as “pretty good and comfortable” and gave the service a 10/10 recommendation.
Ifrita Hossain Muntaha said it was her first bike ride and that having a female rider made the experience more comfortable.
Minhaz Fahim, another customer whose review is published on the website, described the experience as comfortable and recommended the service, while also expressing hope that it would improve further as more people use it.
These reviews are published by Maya Ride as Facebook recommendations from customers, rather than independently conducted interviews.
Maya Ride has also expanded its services beyond individual bike rides.
Its car-sharing service offers women-only shared commutes on selected routes across Dhaka. Passengers can choose pickup-point or door-to-door options, with weekly and monthly packages available on current routes. The platform says drivers are verified and the service is designed for regular office commutes.
Another service, Maya Kids, provides pre-booked transport for school-going children with a verified female companion. The service is aimed at parents who need a more organised option for their children's daily school commute.
The platform is also intended to create income opportunities for women who own motorcycles or cars and want to work as professional drivers.
Fahad said some women are joining the platform not only for income but also because they want to help other women.
“Women are working with the intention of helping other women. Isn't that a beautiful thing?” he said.
However, the platform still faces challenges.
The number of active female riders remains relatively small compared with the demand for rides. This can make it difficult to match passengers with drivers, particularly for certain locations and times. A limited driver network can also increase the cost of rides.
The founders hope that bringing more women into the network will make the service more widely available and help reduce costs over time.
Maya Ride currently operates through its website and booking channels. Its website says customers can request rides for immediate service, subject to rider and vehicle availability, or book for a selected date and time. The company also provides customer support during its operating hours.
For women navigating Dhaka every day, Maya Ride is offering a simple alternative: a journey where the passenger can choose a female rider.
At the same time, the platform is trying to turn women's mobility needs into an opportunity for other women to earn through driving.

item.title: Kobir: PM never ruled out visiting India through proper bilateral framework
item.description:
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on Monday expressed optimism that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman will pay a bilateral visit to India at a convenient time, stressing that the prime minister has never ruled out visiting the country through a proper bilateral framework.
“To maintain relations with another country, bilateral engagement is required. We will do it directly. The visit will be bilateral, and we will talk,” Kobir told reporters after delivering his speech at the Bay of Bengal Conversation in Dhaka.
Kobir said there were challenges in Bangladesh-India relations but expressed optimism that they could be addressed through dialogue.
“There are challenges, but we believe those can be overcome through dialogue,” he said.
Asked about the possibility of the prime minister’s visit to India this year, Kobir said Dhaka wants the visit to take place in a conducive environment and through a proper bilateral framework, but he did not give any specific timeframe.
“Nothing gets resolved just over a phone call. We are having discussions, and things are positive,” the state minister said.
He praised Indian High Commissioner to Bangladesh Dinesh Trivedi for trying to understand Bangladesh’s current context and said Dhaka hoped New Delhi would give due importance to his assessments.
“The Indian high commissioner here is doing a good job; he is trying,” Kobir said.
“Hopefully, Delhi will be receptive to him and the opinions and analysis he provides regarding the context in Bangladesh.”
Bangladesh wants to pursue a foreign policy based on strategic autonomy, national interest and balanced engagement with all countries, he said, stressing that Dhaka will not compromise its national interests while maintaining open channels with its partners.
“Every country wants strategic autonomy. Bangladesh also wants it,” Kobir said while speaking to journalists on the sidelines of the programme.
On the renewal of the Ganges Water Sharing Treaty, which is due to expire in December 2026, Kobir said Bangladesh would seek an outcome that serves its national interests.
The treaty’s expiry in December 2026 has also emerged as a major issue for the two countries.
Asked whether the existing treaty would be renewed or replaced with a new agreement, he said: "Whatever is best for Bangladesh’s interest will be done.”
Asked about a possible guarantee clause, Kobir said Bangladesh would work to safeguard its national interests and security.
“Whatever is best for Bangladesh’s national interest and security, we will work to ensure that,” he said.
Kobir said discussions are already underway and that Bangladesh is waiting for a response from its Indian counterparts.
“Our committee is ready. We are just waiting for the final response from our Indian counterparts. So yes, we are hopeful,” he said.
Kobir said Bangladesh would engage positively with the international community while protecting its national interests.
“We want to engage in a positive way that does not compromise our national interest, yet we embrace the diversity on offer to achieve success politically, economically, and in terms of overall security,” he said.
The state minister said Bangladesh expected India to prevent individuals based in India from using its territory to make political statements or engage in activities aimed at destabilising Bangladesh.
“Restraining a terrorist or extremist in their land is not too much to ask,” he said.
“Why should that happen? So, if that is restrained, there won’t be any issues with our relationship, and a normal working relationship can be maintained, which is essential for both countries.”
He said Bangladesh also would not allow anyone from India to use Bangladeshi territory to make statements against the Indian government.
“We don’t allow any terrorist coming from India to sit here and speak against the Indian government. So, it sends a bad message. We hope India will do that as well,” Kobir said, noting that such restraint would help create a more stable environment for bilateral relations.
Kobir stressed that India remained an important partner for Bangladesh despite existing differences.
“Regional cooperation is required, and India will be an important partner for Bangladesh,” he said.
“As we said, we never close the door to dialogue in diplomacy. It is always open,” Kobir said.
Kobir also linked the government’s foreign policy approach to its broader vision of strategic autonomy, saying Bangladesh would seek engagement with countries across the world without compromising its own interests. “We will engage across the board,” he said.
He said Bangladesh would continue to approach its relationship with India with openness and candidness while seeking solutions to outstanding issues through dialogue.
“We are having positive discussions, and I am hopeful we will reach satisfactory conclusions,” Kobir said.
He also expressed hope that the prime minister’s visit to India would eventually take place once the necessary conditions were in place.
“The prime minister never said no to visiting,” Kobir said. “Certain things need to be addressed. We will reach a positive resolution through talks, and I am hopeful the visit will happen.”

item.title: Fortune Rice Bran Oil promotes Walkathon for heart health
item.description:

item.title: Experts: Bangladesh poultry must shift from volume to value
item.description:
Speakers at the International Technical Seminar 2026 organized by the World's Poultry Science Association – Bangladesh Branch (WPSA-BB) emphasized that Bangladesh's poultry sector must move beyond a volume-centric mindset and focus on farm profitability, food safety, climate resilience, and internationally credible standards.
Held under the theme "Resilient Poultry Production for Global Competitiveness", the seminar featured eight speakers representing the government, industry, and academia.
Md Shahzaman Khan, director general, Department of Livestock Services (DLS), attended the inaugural session as chief guest.
Special guests included Moshiur Rahman, convener, Bangladesh Poultry Industries Central Council (BPICC), and Shakila Faruque, director general, Bangladesh Livestock Research Institute (BLRI).
The session was chaired by WPSA-BB president Shamsul Arefin Khaled.
WPSA-BB president Shamsul Arefin Khaled stated that while the sector has addressed volume growth, it has yet to secure value realization.
Despite rising output, many producers are incurring losses; according to his estimates, breeder farms lost approximately Tk1,706 crore over the past 20 months.
He highlighted that profit margins have shifted from farms and hatcheries to intermediaries along the supply chain.
He urged aligning chick supply with market demand, according legal status to the national poultry policy, and expanding investments in insurance, processing, and cold chains.
Ensuring farmer protection and building a sustainable industry: WPSA-BB general secretary Fayzur Rahman outlined the strategic direction for the industry.
Md Zahidul Islam, director & CEO of Bangla-UK Agro Products Ltd, noted that the lowest FCR does not always yield the highest profitability. Adhering strictly to drug withdrawal periods and marketing heavier birds can improve farm income as well as food safety.
Khitima Jindamongkon, regional manager at dsm-firmenich APAC, shared insights from Asian poultry industries, noting that future success depends on integration, processing, traceability, and leveraging local breeds like the 'Sonali' chicken.
Prof Emdadul Haque Chowdhury, Department of Pathology at Bangladesh Agricultural University (BAU), presented a research study combining consumer/stakeholder surveys with laboratory testing. Contrary to public misconceptions, no growth hormones were detected in the tested samples.
Moshiur Rahman, managing director of Paragon Group and convener of BPICC, stated that optimizing feed conversion, efficient energy management, and reducing mortality can lower both operational costs and carbon emissions.
Baby Rani Karmakar, joint secretary at the Ministry of Fisheries and Livestock, noted that while Bangladesh can compete in international halal markets, success requires internationally recognized certification, accredited laboratories, and market-specific compliance frameworks.
The seminar concluded with an open discussion titled "Towards a Globally Competitive, Safe, and Sustainable Poultry Sector in Bangladesh", moderated by Prof Md Mahmudul Hasan Sikder, member-secretary of the WPSA-BB technical sub-committee.
Discussions also focused on developing affordable, smart, resource-efficient farming models across scales and charting the strategic roadmap for the sector.

item.title: Berger Paints 44th National Women’s Chess Championship begins
item.description:
The Berger Paints 44th National Women’s ‘B’ Chess Championship 2026 officially commenced on Saturday, October 3, at the Bangladesh Chess Federation.
Sponsored by Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited and organized by the Bangladesh Chess Federation, the event brings together 73 players from 22 districts.
Salahuddin Ahmed, chief marketing officer of Berger Paints Bangladesh Limited, inaugurated the tournament as chief guest.
Grandmaster Niaz Murshed, general secretary of the Bangladesh Chess Federation, expressed his gratitude to Berger Paints for supporting women's chess and welcomed the participants.
Key federation officials present at the opening included joint secretary Fide Master Mehdi Hasan Parag, treasurer Mohammad Farhadur Rahman Shabab, international arbiter Md Haroon Or Rashid, and ad hoc committee member Md Monjur Alam.
This year's championship features top players from across the country, including three Women International Masters (WIMs), three Women FIDE Masters (WFMs), and six Women Candidate Masters (WCMs).
The top 12 players from this event will advance to the final stage of the 44th National Women’s Chess Championship.

item.title: Police detain security guard over assault of street child in Mirpur
item.description:
Police have detained a security guard accused of assaulting a street child in Mirpur 1, Dhaka, after allegedly accusing her of stealing a piece of bread.
The detained man has been identified as Ripon Mondol, who works as a security guard at Mirpur Shah Ali Shopping Complex.
In a Facebook post on Monday afternoon, Mirpur Division Additional Deputy Commissioner Saleh Muhammad Zakaria confirmed the detention.
Posting a photo of Ripon Mondol, Saleh Mohammad Zakaria wrote: “The detained man’s name is Ripon Mondol. The night before last, he brutally assaulted a little girl in Mirpur 1. He is now in police custody. He has been admitted to hospital for treatment.”
He further wrote: “The rule of law must be followed. Police will take immediate action in any incident of brutality. There will be no concessions.”
A video showing the street child being assaulted had circulated on social media since Sunday. UK-based Bangladeshi journalist Zulkarnain Saer posted the video on his Facebook account on Monday afternoon.
Posting the video, he wrote: “A security guard at a market somewhere in the Mirpur area is assaulting a girl child on allegations of stealing and eating a piece of bread. When a passer-by approached to stop the assault, another passer-by came forward to prevent him.”
He said: “Whatever the crime, no one has the right to torture anyone. Handing the accused person over to the police is the legal course of action.”
The 15-second video shows a man wearing a navy blue shirt and black full-length trousers holding one of the child’s hands with one hand and beating her with a belt in the other hand on a road in front of a market.
Vehicles can be seen passing nearby while people standing around watch. At one point, several teenagers approach to protect the child, after which the man pulls her towards the market.
Police said the incident took place on Saturday, October 3, in front of Shah Ali Shopping Complex in Mirpur 1.
Ripon Mondol has been detained and is currently undergoing treatment under police guard at the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases and Hospital in Sher-e-Bangla Nagar, Dhaka.
Darus Salam police station Officer-in-Charge Dulal Hossain said: “After the video came to our attention, police began looking into the matter. Ripon Mondol was identified and later questioned.”
Ripon Mondol told police officials that the child had stolen a mobile phone from a shop at the market. He claimed he beat her for this reason.
He was admitted to hospital after suffering a heart attack on Sunday afternoon.
OC Dulal Hossain said: “We are verifying whether Ripon Mondol’s statement is true. He is being kept under police guard at the hospital. Legal action will be taken against him once he recovers. Efforts are underway to locate the street child.”

item.title: Snatcher held with knife at Motijheel Metro Rail Station
item.description:
A snatcher was arrested red-handed at the Entry-A gate of Motijheel Metro Rail Station while allegedly trying to snatch a female passenger’s bag.
The suspect was reportedly intimidating the woman near the station’s lift when Ansar member Md Rakibul Islam, who was on patrol duty, noticed the incident.
Rakibul immediately intervened with APC Rokonuzzaman and Ansar member Shahin Mia and detained the suspect, identified as Zakir Hossain, at the scene.
A search of Zakir’s body led to the recovery of a large sharp knife.
The incident was promptly reported to the station controller. Later, in the controller’s presence, Ansar members handed Zakir and the seized knife over to MRT Police.

item.title: Tourist vehicle plunges into ditch in Thanchi, 2 killed, 5 injured
item.description:
Two people were killed and five others seriously injured when a tourist vehicle, locally known as a “Chander Gari”, plunged into a deep roadside ditch in Thanchi upazila of Bandarban on Monday afternoon.
The identities of the deceased could not be known immediately.
According to Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the accident occurred around 3:45pm on the Dimpahar-Tendumukh road, about 600 meters from the Tendumukh BGB check post.
Personnel of Tendumukh BGB Camp under Bolipara Battalion (38 BGB), led by its commanding officer Lt Col Md Yasir Arafat Hossain, rushed to the spot after receiving information about the accident and launched a rescue operation.
They recovered two people dead from the wreckage and rescued five others in critical condition.
The injured were sent to Alikadam Upazila Health Complex.
BGB informed Thanchi Police Station to take necessary legal steps regarding the bodies of the deceased.
Lieutenant Colonel Md Yasir Arafat Hossain said necessary legal and administrative measures regarding the accident are underway.

item.title: Woman found dead at DMCH identified as BIRDEM staff nurse
item.description:
The woman whose bloodied body was found hanging in a bathroom at Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) has been identified as Tanmoy Mondol, a senior staff nurse at BIRDEM General Hospital in Shahbagh. She had joined the hospital about a month ago.
The incident has taken a mysterious turn after a bloodstained fruit knife and bloodstains were found near the second gate of a conference room in the hospital’s administrative block several hours before her body was discovered. Police and hospital authorities have launched an investigation to determine the actual cause of her death.
Shahbagh Police Station Officer-in-Charge (OC) Mohammad Moniruzzaman said on Monday afternoon that police had recovered the bloodstained knife and were investigating the circumstances surrounding the death.
Asked whether it was a murder, the OC said, “There are many mysteries surrounding the incident. We are trying to uncover them.” He said the deceased had allegedly obtained a mobile SIM card using the national identity card of one of her friends, adding that police were investigating this and other possible leads.
A few hours before the body was found, a bloodstained black steel fruit knife was discovered at around 6:30am in front of the second gate of the conference room in the hospital’s administrative block.
Cleaner Kashi Santosh was the first to spot the knife. He said he cleaned the bloodstained area on the instructions of a senior official, then washed the knife and kept it with him.
About four to five hours later, he learned that a body had been found in the bathroom between wards 110 and 111, although he did not see the woman himself.
DMCH Assistant Director Dr Shayla Ferdous Ahsan said she learned about the hanging body after arriving at the hospital in the morning. She later learned about the bloodstains and knife found near the conference room.
She said blood drops had been found in front of the conference room’s second gate. CCTV footage from the area is being reviewed and may provide important clues to the incident.
Police recovered the body at around 10:30am from cubicle No 4 of the women’s bathroom between wards 110 and 111 of DMCH.
Earlier, at around 10:00am, cleaner Mahmud Sheikh went to clean the bathroom as part of his routine duties. He knocked on the doors of the cubicles and asked the occupants to come out.
When there was no response from cubicle No 4 despite repeated knocking, he became suspicious. With the help of another cleaner, he opened the door and found the woman hanging inside, with blood on her body.
The cleaners then informed Ansar members and senior hospital officials, who subsequently notified Shahbagh police.

item.title: Kane and Bellingham driving England forward after World Cup pain
item.description:
Harry Kane is set to equal England's appearance record with his 125th cap against the Czech Republic on Tuesday as the striker looks to build on his flourishing partnership with "scary" Jude Bellingham.
Kane will take centre stage if he ties former England goalkeeper Peter Shilton's landmark in the Nations League clash at Wembley.
The England captain's pride in representing his country has shone through since his debut against Lithuania in 2015.
Kane scored within two minutes of coming off the bench in that match, and he has rarely endured a barren spell in an England shirt ever since.
The 33-year-old is England's record scorer with 89 goals after netting twice in Saturday's 7-0 demolition of Croatia.
Bayern Munich star Kane has been England's talisman and the one constant throughout their highs and lows over the last 11 years.
Roy Hodgson gave Kane his England debut and the striker has since played under coaches Sam Allardyce, Gareth Southgate, Lee Carsley and now Thomas Tuchel.
But even having a player of Kane's predatory instincts and remarkable consistency has not been enough for England to end their angst-ridden wait for a first major trophy since the 1966 World Cup.
England lost the European Championship final in 2021 and 2024.
And for Kane to follow Bobby Moore as the only male England captain to lift a trophy, Tuchel believes he needs an assist from a midfielder whose virtuoso performance against Croatia on Saturday drew gushing praise from team-mates and pundits alike.
In danger of missing out on the World Cup after being dropped from the England squad in October 2025, Real Madrid star Bellingham has gone from Tuchel's doghouse to the penthouse over the last 12 months.
Having irked Tuchel with his volatile on-pitch antics, Bellingham eventually regained his place in time for the World Cup in June and July.
It was Bellingham rather than Kane who finished as England's top scorer at the World Cup, but their tournament ended in semi-final heartbreak against Argentina.
- 'Never seen anything like it' -
Tuchel's defensive tactics in the closing stage of that loss were widely pilloried.
But has learnt from that late meltdown and wants England to stay on the offensive, with Kane and Bellingham leading the charge.
Key to England's hopes of winning Euro 2028 will be Kane staying healthy and Bellingham remaining in the kind of masterful form that inspired the rout of Croatia.
The 23-year-old was so dominant in Rijeka, scoring once and providing three assists, that former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane said he can go on to be "one of the greatest players of all time".
"At this moment in time, he is an amazing footballer. The package, his running power, his delivery, his goal threat," Keane said.
Keane's praise was echoed by Bournemouth's Alex Scott, who made his first England start alongside Bellingham and Elliot Anderson in midfield against Croatia.
"Honestly, I've never seen anything like it," Scott said.
"He's even better in person, seeing it up close and being on the same pitch as him, he's the best midfielder in the world.
"On the pitch his ability is scary and that's the benchmark we need to live up to."
England winger Bukayo Saka added: "He was special, (I'm) happy to play with him and happy to have him in the England team."
Tuchel said Kane's relationship with Bellingham has blossomed on and off the pitch in recent months, paving the way for the explosion of creativity and goals from the pair.
Fittingly, it was Bellingham who took the captain's armband from Kane when the striker was replaced late in the Croatia match.
"They get better and better. They love playing with each other. They understand each other better," Tuchel said.
"We adjusted our positioning a little bit after the World Cup. Jude almost plays a little bit more offensive for us. That's where I see him in the most dangerous position."

item.title: Spain’s PM calls snap election after housing bill defeat
item.description:
Spain’s Prime Minister on Monday called a snap election for November 29, after parliament rejected housing relief measures proposed by his minority government amid nationwide protests.
The defeat on Friday was just the latest political setback for the Socialist premier Pedro Sanchez, one of the few left-leaning government leaders still in power in the European Union.
“To do more, we need to renew and broaden the support of the people,” Sanchez said in a televised address, adding that his aim was “to secure a much broader, progressive majority in parliament.”
The next general election was scheduled to take place by August 2027.
Sanchez brought the polls forward as protests over Spain’s housing market have ballooned.
His announcement came after tens of thousands of protesters marched in Madrid and other Spanish cities on Saturday to demand action on housing affordability.
The proposed measures, which included automatic renewal of tenancy contracts and restrictions on evicting vulnerable tenants, were voted down by opposition parties in Spain’s parliament.
The defeat infuriated those protesting the country’s increasingly expensive housing market and underscored the difficulties his minority coalition government faces in passing legislation.
The demonstrations were fueled by the eviction last month of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from her Madrid flat, where she had lived for decades.
Hundreds of protesters have occupied a tent city in the heart of Madrid for more than a week, calling for housing reforms.
“This wave of indignation is unstoppable and we are not going to stop,” Alicia del Rio, a spokesperson for the Madrid Tenants’ Union, which has led the protests, said while renewing a call for a general strike.
Recent opinion polls have generally put the main opposition conservative Popular Party (PP) ahead of the Socialists.
The PP would likely need to partner with the far-right Vox to form a government.
Making housing the central campaign issue “could mobilize left-leaning voters,” said Federico Santi, a Europe analyst at political risk consultancy Eurasia Group.
He said an early election could help limit further erosion of support for the Socialists, amid resurgent inflation, legislative deadlock and corruption scandals.
Housing has for years been a top concern for Spaniards as supply falls short of demand, with rents and house prices rising, as elsewhere in the European Union.
Average rents in Spain have almost doubled over the past decade, while asking prices for homes have risen by about 90%, according to real estate website Idealista.
Abascal’s eviction catalyzed long-running anger about runaway housing costs..
The backlash led the corporate new owners of the building that includes her flat to reach a deal allowing her to return at a low rent.
The housing bills were rejected after the Catalan separatist party Junts -- on whose support the government relies -- voted against, arguing they were hastily drawn up and would make the housing crisis worse.
Sanchez, in power since 2018, defended his government’s record in his address on Monday, saying Spain’s economy has grown faster than those of its main European peers and that unemployment had fallen during his tenure.
But after eight years in power, Sanchez is also under pressure over corruption scandals involving people close to him, including his wife and top figures in his Socialist Party.
Sanchez, one of Europe’s chief critics of US President Donald Trump, has also faced widespread criticism over his handling of the crisis in the North African territory of Ceuta, where thousands of migrants from Morocco entered in late July.
Many ordinary Spaniards say they have not felt the benefits of the country’s economic growth, with inflation outpacing wage growth and rent taking up an increasing share of household incomes.
PP leader Alberto Nunez Feijoo welcomed the snap election announcement.
“If eight years have not been enough, why would four more be?” he said.

item.title: US withdraws all bomber aircraft from UK airbase
item.description:
The United States confirmed that it had withdrawn all B-1 bombers from the British airbase of RAF Fairford, reportedly due to “new threats,” with Britain’s government insisting Monday the site is safe.
Police were called to the base in southwest England on September 27 after a local farmer reported a group of men with several vans engaged in “suspicious” activity.
The scare prompted a counter-terrorism probe and forced evacuations at 85 homes near the airbase, which was used by the United States to launch strikes on Iran.
Investigators did not find any explosives in the vans, but “a quantity of petrol was recovered,” according to counter-terrorism police.
A statement from a Pentagon official on Sunday said “we can acknowledge now that all US bombers that were deployed to RAF Fairford have re-deployed to their home stations in the United States.”
The statement noted that “operational security precluded us from confirming the movement of our assets and forces in real-time.”
An unidentified US official told CNN that the bombers were moved after “an unspecified new threat,” with the source calling the latest threat a “real world incident.”
It was unusual to move the bombers back to their home stations instead of deploying them to another base in the region, the official reportedly said.
Two US officials told the New York Times that the bombers were moved after commanders received new threats about an Iran-backed plot against the base.
One American official said the new information was part of the same threat warnings that surfaced three weeks ago, but the situation became urgent in the past 24 hours, the Times reported.
Asked whether the base was safe, UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s official spokesman said: “Yes.”
“We have tried and tested approaches to defend our bases around the country and throughout the world,” he told reporters.
Speculation about the motives behind the incident ranged from terror threat to fuel theft, as energy prices in the UK hit record highs this week.
Burnham has said there were “strong indications that Iran played a part” in the incident, a charge rejected by Tehran.
Six London-based Britons arrested in the September incident, including a UK-Iranian dual national, all men in their mid-20s, were released on bail, drawing rebuke from Washington.
“I wouldn’t have done that,” US President Donald Trump told reporters, as his Secretary of State Marco Rubio alleged a “foreign actor” was involved.
Iran’s embassy in London said it “categorically rejects and strongly condemns” speculation that Tehran was involved.
Adding to the mystery, British media reported that officers were alerted to the incident by one of the initial suspects, but police have not commented on the reports.
Security at the base had reportedly been heightened recently.
Britain gave Washington permission in March to use Fairford for “specific defensive operations into Iran,” and US bombers and other planes have since been seen taking off and landing at the base.
Fairford is the only airbase on Britain’s mainland used for this purpose.
The incident came after a farmer living in the village of Whelford, near the airbase, called the police after seeing three vans blocking a road and a group of masked men fleeing the scene.
Aerial footage of the vans showed they appeared to contain barrels, and at least one was marked with a fake logo and phone number, giving the false impression that it was owned by a legitimate diesel delivery firm.

item.title: India court seeks explanations from election body in voter list row
item.description:
India’s Supreme Court ordered the government and the national election body on Monday to explain decisions linked to a large-scale revision of voter rolls that prompted accusations of wrongdoing.
Opposition parties and activists have organized protests and called for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar, head of the Election Commission of India (ECI), alleging that the revision had improperly removed millions of names from voter lists.
Critics have accused Kumar of acting at the behest of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party.
The ECI, the constitutional body responsible for conducting elections in the world’s largest democracy, has rejected allegations of wrongdoing.
On Monday, a three-judge bench led by Chief Justice Surya Kant issued notices to the government, the ECI and Kumar after hearing petitions challenging decisions linked to the voter list revision.
Another hearing is expected to be held next week.
One of the petitions sought a probe into ECI records to determine whether its decisions complied with constitutional requirements.
Protests have been held across several cities since a report last month by The Indian Express, which said two of the ECI’s three members had formally objected at least 14 times to key decisions linked to the voter roll revision.
“Newspaper reports may be 100% correct, partially correct or incorrect. We cannot pass an order on that basis today. We would definitely want their response. If we find there were instances where law wasn’t followed, we can undo it,” broadcaster NDTV quoted the bench as saying.
The ECI says the revision exercise, which started last year, is intended to identify fraudulently registered voters and prevent “foreign illegal immigrants” from voting.
Critics say the drive has disproportionately affected marginalized and minority communities, especially Muslims.
India’s main opposition Congress party has announced a protest march to the Election Commission’s offices in New Delhi on Tuesday, to be followed by nationwide “Save Democracy” rallies.
Among those joining the protests are supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a satirical political movement that emerged online in May and succeeded in its campaign to oust the then education minister.
The group has called for a “mass mobilization” in the capital on Saturday.
Police have maintained a heavy presence around the government-designated protest area near New Delhi’s Jantar Mantar, and dozens of demonstrators were briefly detained over the weekend.

item.title: Fans of Brazil’s Lula hope for comeback against Bolsonaro
item.description:
Supporters of Brazilian leader Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva clung to hope on Sunday after right-wing senator Flavio Bolsonaro gained the upper hand in the first round of Brazil’s presidential election to force a runoff.
Bolsonaro, son of the far-right former president Jair Bolsonaro, won 47% of the vote against Lula’s 45%.
Paulista Avenue, the main artery of Sao Paulo and typically a site for celebrations by Lula supporters, had a subdued mood on Sunday night.
Gustavo Maximiliano walked down the avenue worried, though he said he was confident that Lula would win the runoff on October 25.
“The comeback starts now,” the 42-year-old filmmaker told AFP.
“All of Lula’s elections are tough and tight, but he always wins in the second round.”
That was what happened in the three elections in which Lula won the presidency, including in 2022 when he beat Jair Bolsonaro.
Red t-shirts, the color of the president’s Workers’ Party, stayed largely hidden under jackets.
In a statement to the media, Lula acknowledged that he had expected to win in the first round, but promised to prevail “in overtime.”
Aline Araujo, a 33-year-old bank employee, said she is convinced the president will be able to draw on his more than half a century of political experience against the 45-year-old Bolsonaro, who was a little-known senator until a few months ago.
“I still trust Lula. I’m with Lula until the end,” she said.
“Lula knows how to play better,” said Marcos Souza, 29, warning that “you can’t downplay” the fact that “the far right has enormous strength.”
Lula will have three weeks to flip the result in a country that appears to want change.
Workers’ Party President Edinho Silva told reporters that the campaign’s strategy will be to “confront projects and call on Brazil to reflect.”

item.title: Plan International: Climate shocks disrupt girls’ education, health, safety
item.description:
Climate-related disasters are increasing the risks of child marriage, unintended pregnancy and violence among girls while disrupting their access to education and essential health services, a new global study by Plan International has found.
The report, "State of the World’s Girls 2026: Change Her Forecast", draws on research involving more than 5,000 girls and young women aged 15 to 24 in Bangladesh, Kenya, Peru, Senegal and Zimbabwe, alongside an analysis of climate and health data from 52 low- and middle-income countries spanning three decades.
The findings show that climate shocks such as floods, droughts, cyclones and extreme heat are putting additional pressure on families and communities and disrupting the systems girls depend on for their health, safety and education.
Nine in 10 girls surveyed said climate-related events were placing serious pressure on their families’ survival, health and stability.
Meanwhile, 76% said girls and young women in their communities were struggling to access at least one sexual or reproductive health service following climate-related events.
The study found that 36% of girls had seen more girls marry or enter unions before the age of 18 in their communities following climate-related disasters, while 33% reported seeing an increase in unintended pregnancies.
Another 28% observed an increase in violence against women and girls following climate-related events.
The disruption extends to menstrual health. Half of the girls surveyed said girls and young women in their communities were struggling to access menstrual products or clean water needed to manage menstruation.
The report also highlights how climate shocks can make sexual and reproductive healthcare harder to reach, including contraception, maternity care, menstrual health support, counselling and other essential services.
In Bangladesh, 19-year-old Shahina, who participated in the research, described how climate-related economic hardship can contribute to early marriage.
She said: “When floods leave people completely destitute, families think about financial hardship and marry off girls at a very young age.”
According to the report, girls also face increased risks of sexual exploitation after climate-related disasters when protection systems and support networks break down. Some girls reported being pressured to exchange sex for money or basic necessities.
Emergency shelters can also become unsafe, with girls reporting harassment and sexual violence in overcrowded and poorly lit conditions.
The research identifies education as one of the strongest protective factors for girls during climate crises.
Girls whose education is disrupted are twice as likely to marry young or experience an unintended pregnancy, according to the report.
Schools provide girls with education as well as access to information about their rights, health and available services, while also providing support networks that can help protect them from exploitation and early marriage.
The report also highlights the particular risks associated with prolonged drought.
An analysis covering 52 countries over three decades found prolonged drought to be the climate hazard most consistently associated with increasing rates of child marriage and early unions.
As drought destroys crops, livestock and household income over time, families facing financial hardship may resort to marrying off their daughters, the report said.
Reena Ghelani, chief executive officer of Plan International, said: “Girls cannot continue to be treated as an afterthought in climate action. They must have a meaningful say in the decisions that shape their lives, and their rights and needs must be built into climate policy and financing from the outset.”
Ghelani also said climate change was already affecting girls’ education and access to health services.
She added: “Only half of national climate plans mention girls’ or women’s health, and despite the escalating impact of climate shocks on the health systems and services girls rely on, just 0.5% of multilateral climate finance supports health.”
The report calls on governments and donors to keep schools open and free during climate shocks and allocate a defined share of climate adaptation finance to adolescent girls’ health, including sexual and reproductive health services, contraception and maternity care.
It also recommends that menstrual products, contraception and protection services be included in emergency response packages from the beginning rather than being treated as later interventions.
Plan International further called for targeted support for girls from minority communities, girls with disabilities and those already displaced, who face greater barriers to accessing essential services.
The organisation urged governments and donors to put girls at the centre of climate policy, financing and disaster response, arguing that their experiences and leadership should help shape decisions affecting their lives.
The report comes ahead of COP31, where countries are expected to negotiate further international action on climate change.

item.title: Attack on New Gini Properties: Maj Gen (retd) Mohiuddin gets bail
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Monday granted bail to Major General (retd) Golam Mohiuddin Chowdhury in a case filed over the attack, vandalism and looting at a New Gini Properties housing project, including at content creator Salman Mohammad Muqtadir's "Brownfish Studio", in the South Manikdi area of the capital.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid passed the order after hearing a bail petition filed by the defense.
The court granted him bail on a Tk 2,000 bond until the next scheduled date, according to his lawyers.
The next date for submitting the investigation report in the case has been set for October 28.
Golam Mohiuddin was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police from a house in the capital's Segunbagicha area on September 30.
New Gini Properties Director Saiful Islam Bhuiyan filed the case with Cantonment Police Station over the attack on the housing project near the ECB Chattar on the night of September 26.
Salman Muqtadir's "Brownfish Studio", located inside the housing project, was also attacked, vandalized and looted.
According to the case statement, a group of people, equipped with weapons, entered the project area and opened fire before attacking with machetes, knives and sticks. At one stage, they entered Salman Muqtadir's studio and vandalized and looted it.
The complaint alleged that cash, laptops, computers, cameras, professional media equipment and other valuables were looted, while vehicles were also vandalized.
Several people, including site engineer Md Parvez, were injured in the attack.
The complainant alleged that the incident caused losses of around Tk 1.42 crore to the company and that goods worth Tk 1.50 crore were allegedly stolen.
Thirteen people were named in the case, while another 150 to 200 unidentified people were accused.

item.title: Lightning strike leaves 18 students ill at Gazipur school
item.description:
At least 18 students fell ill after lightning struck near Singua Bahumukhi High School in Kapasia upazila of Gazipur on Monday afternoon.
The affected students were taken to Monohardi Upazila Health Complex in neighbouring Narsingdi for treatment. The incident occurred around noon while classes were underway at the school.
Local residents said heavy rain began in the afternoon, followed by several lightning strikes. Hearing students crying from the school’s ground floor, residents rushed to the building and found several students lying on the floor and benches in an almost unconscious state.
Headteacher Mostafizur Rahman said several consecutive lightning strikes occurred around 2:00pm, leaving at least 18 female students on the ground floor sick.
Teachers and local residents took the affected students to Monohardi Upazila Health Complex. Six were admitted for treatment, while the others were sent home after receiving first aid.
A Matin, a senior staff nurse at the health complex, said six students had been admitted and were receiving treatment. The others were discharged after receiving primary treatment.

item.title: IPDC Finance receives ADFIAP Development Award 2026 for e-Nothi initiative

IPDC Finance PLC has won the Award in Technology Development at the ADFIAP Development Awards 2026 for its digital transformation initiative, e-Nothi.
The award was presented at the 49th ADFIAP Annual Meetings, held in Colombo, Sri Lanka, from September 23 to 25, 2026.
Representing IPDC Finance, Barrister Samiul Hashim, company secretary, head of legal affairs and acting head of brand & corporate communication, and Md Afzalur Rashid, chief technology officer, received the award at the ceremony.
